  1. Description

Annotation Interface TomlConfig

@Documented @Retention(CLASS) @Target(TYPE) public @interface TomlConfig
Marks a record that documents bind to, with Toml.parse(String, Class) or Toml.bind(TomlTable, Class). 
@TomlConfig
record AppConfig(String title, Server server, List<Endpoint> endpoints) {}
record Server(String host, int port, @Nullable Duration timeout) {}
record Endpoint(String path, Set<String> methods) {}

AppConfig config = Toml.parse(file, AppConfig.class);

The annotation processor of the be.imgn.toml:toml-processor artifact generates the code that binds a table to the record, and registers it as a TomlBinder service. It rejects at compile time a type it cannot bind. The records the record refers to are bound the same way, without the annotation.

Each component of a record is the value of a key of the table, in kebab case: timeoutSeconds is the value of timeout-seconds. TomlKey gives another key. A key the table lacks is an error, unless the component is annotated @Nullable, which makes it null. A key of the table that no component takes is an error too, unless the table is bound with UnknownKeys.IGNORE.

The values are bound as follows; anything else is an error, reported as a TomlMappingException:

  • String, from a string;
  • long, int, short and byte, from an integer in their range;
  • double and float, from a float, or from an integer they represent exactly;
  • boolean, from a boolean;
  • OffsetDateTime, LocalDateTime, LocalDate and LocalTime, from the date-time of the same kind;
  • an enum, from a string naming a constant in kebab case: READ_ONLY is "read-only", unless the constant has a TomlKey;
  • Duration, from a string in ISO-8601, as "PT1M30S", or of amounts with units, as "1m30s" (see TomlBindings.asDuration(TomlValue, TomlBindings.Context));
  • Path, from a string, on the default file system;
  • URI, from a string;
  • List<T> and Set<T>, from an array of values that bind to T; a set rejects duplicates;
  • Map<String, T>, from a table of values that bind to T, whatever their keys;
  • a record, from a table;
  • TomlValue and its subtypes, as they are.

The boxed types of the primitive types bind as the primitive types. Lists, sets and maps keep the order of the document, and cannot be modified.

Toml.toTable(Record) converts a record back to a table, in the forms above.
